Cabinet Painting Prices Across Sugar Land, Missouri City, Richmond, Katy, Fulshear, Rosenberg & West Houston

Most homeowners invest between $2,000 and $10,000+ depending on cabinet size, condition, and finish level.

Cabinet painting is one of the most detail-intensive painting projects in your home.

The difference between a finish that lasts and one that fails comes down to prep, process, and

product — not just paint.

Cabinet Painting Price Ranges

Most cabinet projects fall into these ranges:

Small Kitchen (10–20 doors/drawers)

$2,000 – $4,000

Medium Kitchen (20–40 doors/drawers)

$4,000 – $7,000

Large Kitchen (40+ doors/drawers or complex layouts)

$7,000 – $10,000+

Final pricing depends on prep requirements, cabinet condition, finish expectations, and the level of detail involved.

Why Cabinet Painting Costs More Than Walls

Cabinet painting is not the same as painting walls.

It requires significantly more prep, precision, and controlled application.

What makes cabinets more labor-intensive:

  • Removing and reinstalling doors and hardware

  • Cleaning and degreasing surfaces

  • Detailed sanding and surface prep

  • Priming for adhesion and durability

  • Controlled spraying for a smooth finish

  • Multiple coats with proper drying time

This is why cabinet painting costs more — and why shortcuts lead to peeling, chipping, and early failure.

What To Expect For Your Painting Project

Our Cabinet Painting Process

This is where the difference is made.

Step 1: Remove & Label

We carefully remove doors, drawers, and hardware, labeling everything for precise reinstallation.

Step 2: Deep Cleaning & Prep

Cabinets are degreased, sanded, and prepped to ensure proper adhesion.

Step 3: Surface Repair

We address minor imperfections and prepare surfaces for a smooth finish.

Step 4: Prime

A bonding primer is applied to create a strong foundation.

Step 5: Spray Finish Application

We use a controlled spray system to achieve a smooth, factory-like finish.

Step 6: Curing & Reinstallation

Doors are cured properly before being reinstalled and adjusted.

What Affects Cabinet Painting Cost

Several factors determine where your project falls within the price range:

  • Number of doors and drawers

  • Cabinet condition (damage, wear, previous coatings)

  • Wood type and surface texture

  • Color change (especially dark to light)

  • Finish level expectations

  • Layout complexity (islands, built-ins, detailed trim)

  • Hardware removal and reinstallation

View Our Cabinet Painting Testimonials

Spray Finish vs Brush & Roll

Not all cabinet painting is equal.

Brush & Roll Finish

  • Lower cost

  • Visible texture

  • Faster application

  • Shorter lifespan

Spray Finish (Our Standard)

  • Smooth, factory-like appearance

  • More durable finish

  • Better coverage and consistency

  • Longer-lasting results

This is one of the biggest differences between low-cost cabinet jobs and professional results.

What’s Included in Our Cabinet Painting Estimates

Clear scope. No surprises.

Timeline Expectations

Cabinet painting is more involved than standard painting.

Most projects take 3–7 days, depending on size and complexity.

We coordinate the process to minimize disruption while allowing proper curing time for a durable finish.

Every kitchen is different. The best way to get an accurate number is with a detailed walkthrough.

We’ll evaluate your cabinets, explain your options, and provide a clear, written estimate.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does cabinet paint last?

With proper prep and products, cabinet finishes can last 7–10+ years.

Can you paint over stained cabinets?

Yes — with proper sanding, priming, and prep.

Do you remove cabinet doors?

Yes. Doors and drawers are removed, labeled, and sprayed separately.

Will my kitchen be unusable?

There will be some disruption, but we plan the process to keep it manageable.

What kind of paint do you use?

We use high-performance cabinet coatings designed for durability and adhesion.
